Keysight Technologies Inc reported revenue of 1.85 billion dollars for the quarter ended 2026-07-31, up 36.54 percent from a year earlier, and net income of 397 million dollars, up 107.85 percent [D1]. Gross margin was 65.87 percent and net margin was 21.51 percent in that quarter [D1]. Earnings per share of 2.82 beat the 2.16 estimate by 30.56 percent [D1]. The Communications Solutions Group contributed 1,345 million dollars of revenue and the Electronic Industrial Solutions Group 501 million dollars [D1]. Guidance for the fourth fiscal quarter is revenue of 1.93 billion to 1.95 billion dollars, about 37 percent growth at the mid-point, and earnings per share of 3.34 to 3.40 dollars on a weighted diluted share count of 172 million [D1].

What the market is arguing about is what happens next rather than what was reported, and the evidence is the reaction, with the shares moving -6.32 percent in the session after the 2026-08-18 release, on 2026-08-19, despite the 30.56 percent earnings surprise [D1]. Management's own framing puts supply rather than demand at the centre, describing the supply environment as less flexible than a year earlier and saying supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue for the next several quarters [D3]. The same call flagged that one-time tariff impacts pulled up fiscal 2026 profitability and will not repeat, which raises the comparison bar [D3]. Management also said demand is far exceeding its ability to supply, that the pipeline continues to grow strongly, and that wireline revenue exceeded wireless revenue for the first time [D3].

The plan is therefore to mark the company against the fourth-quarter figures it set for itself, revenue of 1.93 billion to 1.95 billion dollars and earnings per share of 3.34 to 3.40 dollars, rather than against the prior-year comparison alone [D1]. A second marker is whether supply stops governing conversion, since management said demand is not the limiter and that supply will govern the ability to convert demand into revenue for the next several quarters [D3]. A third is the base effect of the one-time tariff impacts that lifted fiscal 2026 profitability and will not repeat [D4]. A fourth is segment mix, with Communications Solutions Group revenue of 1,345 million dollars and Electronic Industrial Solutions Group revenue of 501 million dollars as the reference points for the quarter ended 2026-07-31 [D1]. A fifth is whether the cost synergies from recent acquisitions are realized on a run-rate basis exiting the fiscal year [D3].

Revenue at or below the 1.93 billion dollars low end of that range, or earnings per share at or below 3.34 dollars, would confirm the reading behind the -6.32 percent session move on 2026-08-19 [D1]. Revenue inside 1.93 billion to 1.95 billion dollars and earnings per share inside 3.34 to 3.40 dollars, with conversion no longer described as supply limited, would support the demand case management set out around the 2026-08-18 release [D3].
